newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets Coahuila natural gas distribution site.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets Coahuila natural gas distribution site.

text.p: Mexico's Energy Regulatory Commission on Monday made public the borders of a natural gas distribution zone around the northern border cities of Ciudad Piedras and Nava in Coahuila state.

Companies and international consortiums have been invited by the government to bid for the right to distribute natural gas in certain zones in the north of the country. Mexican Compania Nacional de Gas has already expressed interest in the Coahuila region, but formal bidding has not yet begun.

The area lies about 130 miles (240 kilometers) west of San Antonio, Texas, with a growing population of about 115,000 residents, which could increase to 224,095 people by 2012, according to the latest census.
"Piedras Negras is absorbing and attracting population because of the maquiladora industry development in the past 20 years," said the notice published in the Official Gazette.
Piedras Negras trades with the United States through neighboring Eagle Pass, Texas, and houses 169 manufacturing establishments and 1,964 businesses dedicated to trade and services, the notice said.

The region receives natural gas imported from the United States and from national oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) gas ducts. Potential fuel consumption is estimated at "1.5 billion kilocalories per day."

The northeast region of Coahuila state is the latest in a series of metropolitan areas designated by the government in a move to increase use of natural gas, cutting down on more polluting fuels. Most Mexican cities do not have a widespread natural gas distribution network.
